subject: EU private deployment — data routing limits, customer KMS escrow options, and subprocessor visibility
messages:
From: elena.moretti@novabank.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: rajiv.singh@novabank.com, lena.hoffmann@novabank.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private deploy questions re: key custody and operator access

Kimberly / Jordan —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Our security and legal teams reviewed the proposed private deployment model and have three immediate questions before we move to procurement:

1) KMS custody model: can NovaBank retain sole control of the customer master key (CMK) in our HSM, or is Redwood requesting an escrow copy for break-glass? If escrow is required, what triggers Redwood access and who authorizes it?

2) Subprocessor routing and telemetry: we need a guarantee that inference traffic and logs for NovaBank will never traverse or get processed by non-EU subprocessors. Can you provide an explicit subprocessor list and routing assurances (region locks / IP whitelisting)?

3) On-prem operator access: describe the exact operator privileges required to patch/upgrade the runtime in an air-gapped on-prem deployment. Will operators need decryption access to cached prefixes or KV stores?

I've attached our KMS requirements matrix (nova-kms-requirements.xlsx) and requested you review the DPA draft you shared (redwood-dpa-draft-v2.pdf).

Appreciate a concise matrix of answers and any changes we should expect in the DPA.

Best,
Elena Moretti
DPO, NovaBank


From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: elena.moretti@novabank.com, rajiv.singh@novabank.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, lena.hoffmann@novabank.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 12:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions re: key custody and operator access

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. See inline answers below and attached an annotated architecture diagram (ringfence-architecture-annotated.png) that maps our proposed controls to each ask. High-level summary:

- Customer-controlled CMK: Yes — NovaBank can retain the CMK in your HSM/KMS. Redwood supports Bring-Your-Own-Key where the CMK never leaves your control. We do not require a copy for routine operations.

- Escrow / break-glass: We offer an optional, customer-managed escrow workflow. If you opt in, Redwood will only request escrow access under a mutually agreed incident playbook (e.g., full site loss AND customer-signed authorization). Requests are logged, auditable, and require two internal Redwood approvers plus customer confirmation. The DPA addendum covers the authorization flow.

- Operator privileges: For on-prem air-gapped installs, Redwood operators do not get default decryption rights to customer data. Patches and runtime upgrades can be applied via signed bundles that do not require unlocking the CMK. There are two exceptional cases where an operator may need temporary access to decrypted artifacts (corrupt KV cache recovery, or lawful e-discovery support), and those actions require a break-glass request and explicit customer approval.

- Subprocessor routing: We will provide an exportable subprocessor list restricted to the EU for this deployment. Additionally, we support IP allowlists and explicit regional routing policies that keep traffic within chosen AZs.

Next steps I propose: (1) Jordan and Marcus can produce a concise matrix mapping each Nova requirement to a control and any DPA language change; (2) we'll capture the escrow authorization flow in an addendum and show it to your legal team; (3) schedule a short technical runbook review with your infra/security team.

I've pasted Jordan and Marcus to action items below.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ringfence-architecture-annotated.png (diagram)
From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions re: key custody and operator access

Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks — attaching a short controls matrix (excerpt below) and a DPA redline we propose for the escrow section. I'll upload the full matrices to the Drive link after this message.

--- Controls excerpt ---
1) Key custody: BYOK (customer CMK) supported. Redwood has no retained copy of the CMK unless customer elects escrow.
2) Escrow (optional): - Escrow holder: customer-managed HSM (preferred) or third-party escrow (customer-selected). - Unlock triggers: catastrophic loss of customer HSM, verified via multi-party attestation. - Authorization: documented customer sign-off + two Redwood SOC approvers.
3) Operator access: - Patch delivery: signed tarball applied by local admin; no operator decryption required. - Runtime diagnostics: metadata only. For cache rehydration, we surface encrypted blobs and require customer-run unlock operations.
4) Subprocessors & routing: - All subprocessors for this engagement will be EU-based vendors; routing locked to EU regions. - Telemetry: anonymized metrics only; customer logs remain within the Nova deployment (configurable retention).

--- DPA redline summary ---
- Added explicit escrow authorization flow (Section 4.2.1).
- Added routing guarantee for EU-only subprocessors (Appendix B).
- Strengthened operator access language and break-glass approvals (Appendix C).

I will send the Drive link with the full XLS and the redline in the next email (expected EOD CET).

-jordan
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: rajiv.singh@novabank.com

Cc: elena.moretti@novabank.com, lena.hoffmann@novabank.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 07:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions re: key custody and operator access

Kimberly / Jordan —

Appreciate the detail. A couple follow-ups from infra: 

- Can you confirm whether cache blobs (KV cache, prefix cache) are ever stored unencrypted on local disks during runtime upgrades? If yes, we need clarification on wipe/rotation semantics.
- For the escrow flow, NovaBank prefers a third-party escrow with strict access controls rather than Redwood holding any copy. Can you circulate a template escrow contract?

Also procurement wants to understand whether opting out of escrow affects pricing or SLAs. 

Thanks,
Rajiv Singh
Head of Infrastructure Security, NovaBank
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: rajiv.singh@novabank.com, elena.moretti@novabank.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 13:44:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions re: key custody and operator access

Rajiv / Elena —

Short answers:

- Cache storage: runtime stores cache blobs encrypted at rest with a per-deployment data key. During upgrades we never write plaintext cache to disk. Upgrades use an atomic swap of encrypted shards; there is a zero-downtime migration path we use in EU private installs. We will document wipe/rotation procedures in the runbook (attached as part of the Drive folder).

- Escrow: we support third-party escrow; I'll attach a standard escrow template in the Drive upload. Choosing escrow is orthogonal to pricing — it's an optional professional-services + legal addendum. There is no automatic SLA degradation if you decline escrow.

Action: I'll add explicit cache-rotation steps to the runbook and include a note in the DPA addendum.

Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
